capabilities: Run OpenCode, Claude Code, and Codex agents on vault notes with user-controlled permissions
Organize ongoing work into Projects with instructions, context, and chat history
Save repeatable prompts as Commands runnable from the editor and command palette
Ask questions about selected text with Quick Ask without leaving the note
Choose between hosted, bring-your-own-key, or local models
extras: Freemium: the plugin frontend is open source and usable free with your own agent accounts or keys, but hosted models, cloud-backed tools, and multi-agent mode require paid Brevilabs licenses. Agent runs only on desktop because its backends are local processes; Quick Chat and Quick Ask work on mobile. Detailed privacy disclosure explains where prompts and context are processed.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to run AI agents that can read notes, use tools, create files, and carry out multi-step tasks across a vault.

relations.evidence: Copilot V4 brings OpenCode, Claude Code, and Codex into Obsidian
Claude Code: Connect an existing installation. Copilot detects common install locations

requires.name: Provider API key for BYOK models
Copilot account for hosted features and paid plans
Copilot Plus or higher license for hosted models and multi-agent

summary: AI assistant plugin that runs agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode inside the vault for multi-step research, writing, and knowledge work.
